graphPresentation.placement: Separate knowledge-connections section after the same-case update proof; not a fourth primary showcase step.
graphPresentation.scope: Restored complete user-provided real-data viewport, dated 2026-09-06. User-attested provenance, not an independently validated graph database or accuracy metric.
graphPresentation.annotations: Localized HTML callouts illustrate AI memory research comparing Mem0/Zep/Letta, Claude/Codex workflows using handoff/recall, and Wenlan development covering wiki pages/citations/MCP. Per user correction, the tool-workflow leader points to the lower-left blue node at 22.3% / 82%, not the visibly named Wenlan MCP cluster. Seven small secondary labels illustrate personal topics: a Japan trip, English practice, AI tools, reading, writing, yearly planning and photography. Reading, writing and language learning remain visible at every width; other secondary topics appear from 1024px upward. The separate fictional email-assistant case is not used as a graph topic. Annotations do not verify captured node contents. The visible caption identifies this distinction. Original screenshot bytes and labels are unchanged; the full-size viewer opens the unannotated image.
graphPresentation.legend: Localized static HTML legend above the capture groups its project/technology/organization/person/theme types as entities/topics, followed by wiki pages and memories. Swatches retain the capture's light-theme palette in either website theme. Connection lines are labeled as relationships. A compact Page sources row lists files (PDF/Markdown), notes and AI conversations separately from the node-color key; it does not invent a file/source node kind. This is a reading aid, not a functional graph filter. The reading question and short purpose sentence occupy separate paragraphs; legend groups align to a shared grid. Equal-width desktop callouts have numbered markers and distinct leader lines; below 768px those markers map to the text key under the image.
